landmarks.name: The Church
landmarks.content: Confessional Lutheranism subscribes to the Book of Concord quia — because it agrees with Scripture. Doctrine does not override exegesis; exegesis drives doctrine.

landmarks.name: Luther's Rose
landmarks.content: A black cross on a red heart, set in a white rose, on a sky-blue field, ringed in gold. Each element carries its own weight: the cross is black because it mortifies; the heart remains red because faith keeps it alive.

landmarks.name: Book of Concord
landmarks.content: The Book of Concord (1580) collects the confessional writings of the Lutheran church. Subscription is quia — because these documents agree with Scripture — not quatenus, insofar as they agree. The distinction is load-bearing.

landmarks.name: The Font
landmarks.content: Matter matters. The water of baptism is not merely symbolic — God works through physical means. Sacramental realism: creation, body, and institution carry genuine theological weight.

landmarks.name: Daily Vocation
landmarks.content: Faithful presence in ordinary roles is the frame. Not activism, not transformation — the work of each station done well. The Lutheran doctrine of vocation dignifies the everyday.

landmarks.name: The Missouri Synod
landmarks.content: The LCMS is a confessional Lutheran church body in the United States, committed to the inerrancy of Scripture and the Lutheran Confessions. It is the denominational home of this faith.
